gaps.sentence: The island is ___ , with no permanent residents (HABIT).
gaps.explanation: 'No permanent residents' shows the negative: uninhabited (un- + inhabited). An adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: Her kindness and ___ (GENEROUS) made her very popular.
gaps.explanation: Parallel to 'kindness', a noun is needed: generosity (note the irregular -osity spelling).

gaps.sentence: He felt he was ___ for the work he did, so he asked for a raise (PAY).
gaps.hint: paid too little — he wants a raise (under-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix under- means too little: underpaid means paid less than deserved, which explains asking for a raise.

gaps.sentence: The training course will ___ you to work abroad (QUALIFY).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: qualify. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.hint: person needed (-ist for fields of study)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ist forms the person who studies a subject: biology becomes biologist.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (PROSPER) of the region depends on tourism.
The article was full of ___ information (ACCURATE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'information'
gaps.explanation: The negative adjective 'inaccurate' (in- + accurate) modifies the noun 'information'.
